name: Azure OpenAI
tagline: OpenAI models such as GPT run by Microsoft in its Azure cloud, used by developers to build their own apps

evidence.quote: This Microsoft Online Subscription Agreement is between the entity you represent
and Microsoft Corporation ("Microsoft", "we", "us", or "our")

vendor_entity.note: Contracting party in the online (pay-as-you-go) Azure subscription agreement. Institutions buying through an Enterprise Agreement or Microsoft Customer Agreement in their region may contract with a regional Microsoft affiliate; those agreement texts were not readable here.

evidence.quote: Microsoft Corporation, One Microsoft Way, Redmond, Washington 98052

parent_company.note: Microsoft Corporation is itself the top-level company; no owner above it is named in the privacy statement, DPA or subscription agreement. OpenAI supplies the models but does not own or operate the service (data privacy page: models do not interact with services operated by OpenAI).

parent_country.note: No separate parent company (see Parent company); the vendor country applies.

eu_representative.note: Named in the DPA "How to Contact Microsoft" section. The privacy statement also gives Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited as the EEA contact.

evidence.quote: Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited, Attn: Data Protection Officer, One Microsoft Place, South County Business Park, Leopardstown, Dublin 18, Ireland.

dpo_contact.note: A DPO is reachable by address (and the privacy web form); no DPO is named as a person.

evidence.quote: Is stored at rest in the Foundry resource in the customer's Azure tenant, within the same geography as the resource
any data stored at rest, such as uploaded data, and including the abuse monitoring data store created for Global and DataZone deployments, is stored in the customer-designated geography

hosting_regions.note: Storage follows the Azure region the customer picks for the resource; EU is the answer for an institution that creates its resource in an EU region. Processing location depends on deployment type (see EU residency).
hosting_regions.footnote: Customers choose the region; resources can equally be created in the US, APAC or other Azure geographies.

evidence.quote: Microsoft hosts the Models sold by Azure in Microsoft's Azure environment

local_first.note: Cloud API only; no local or on-device mode found.

evidence.quote: Data Zone types: The service processes data only within the Microsoft-specified data zone (US, EU, or Asia Pacific (APAC)).
For any deployment type labeled 'Global,' prompts and responses may be processed in any geography where the relevant model sold by Azure is deployed

eu_residency.note: Chosen per deployment: Standard (regional) and DataZone EU keep processing in the EU; Global deployments (and Batch, which is Global) may process prompts outside the EU while stored data stays in the chosen geography. For EU deployments, human abuse reviewers are in the EEA.

evidence.quote: Models sold by Azure are also hosted by Azure and operated by Azure as part of the Foundry Models service.
are subject to the terms of the 2021 Standard Contractual Clauses implemented by Microsoft

Microsoft Online Services Subprocessors

subprocessors_public.note: Published on the Service Trust Portal. The edition that could be downloaded is dated February 28, 2025; the current 2026-11-04 edition listed on the portal could not be opened.

subprocessors_count.note: Current (2026-11-04) list not readable. The readable edition dated 2025-02-28 lists 46 distinct third-party companies (7 integrated-technology, 6 ancillary, 33 contract-staff firms; Accenture counted once), plus Microsoft datacenter group entities not counted. Most entries apply only to specific services (e.g. Azure Maps, Databricks); the list does not single out Azure OpenAI.

subprocessors_non_eea.note: Current list not readable. In the 2025-02-28 edition most third-party subprocessors are US-headquartered and list US or worldwide processing; not counted because the current edition could not be checked.

evidence.quote: Last Updated: November 2026

privacy_policy_date.note: Microsoft Privacy Statement gives month only. The Azure OpenAI data, privacy and security page was last updated 2026-06-05; the DPA is dated November 1, 2026.

evidence.quote: Microsoft will temporarily store Input and Output Content
Can be deleted by the customer at any time.

retention_stated.note: Prompts and outputs kept for abuse monitoring are stored "temporarily" with no period stated in the pages read. Data stored for features (files, Responses API, threads, stored completions, fine-tuning) stays until the customer deletes it.

evidence.quote: Microsoft will retain Customer Data that remains stored in Online Services in a limited function account for 90 days after expiration or termination
Customer Data and Personal Data stored in Online Services within an additional 90 days

deletion_on_exit.note: 90 days for extraction, then deletion within a further 90 days (excludes free trials).

data_export.note: The DPA gives a 90-day post-termination window to extract data and EU Data Act export rights, but no export format for Azure OpenAI content is stated in the pages read.

governing_law.note: Washington State law under the online subscription agreement (US version). Enterprise or regional agreements may name other law; not read. The DPA GDPR Terms are governed by EU or Member State law.

are NOT available to OpenAI or other providers of Models sold by Azure.

ai_providers.note: OpenAI-developed models hosted and operated by Microsoft; they do not call OpenAI's own services.

evidence.quote: are NOT used to train any generative AI foundation models without your permission or instruction.
Microsoft Generative AI Services will not use Customer Data to train any generative AI foundation model, except pursuant to Customer’s documented instructions.

trains_on_content.note: Also: not used by model providers to improve their models, and not used to improve Microsoft or third-party products without explicit permission. Fine-tuning on customer data happens only when the customer runs it, and the fine-tuned model is only for that customer.

evidence.quote: Microsoft will temporarily store Input and Output Content
If the customer has been approved for modified abuse monitoring (learn more at Abuse Monitoring )), the data storage and human review process described above is not performed.

ai_zero_retention.note: By default flagged prompts and outputs can be stored for human abuse review in the resource's geography. Customers approved under Limited Access for modified abuse monitoring avoid that storage (automated review still runs). The models themselves are stateless.

evidence.quote: Azure OpenAI supports Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC), an authorization system for managing individual access to Azure resources.

ai_admin_off.note: The whole service is AI; there is no separate AI toggle. Admins control who can use a resource through Azure RBAC (and Azure Policy), or do not create the resource.

evidence.quote: Microsoft is committed to building products and solutions that comply with the EU AI Act and helping our customers use AI compliantly.

ai_act_statement.note: Microsoft-wide Trust Center page, not specific to Azure OpenAI. Microsoft also publishes a transparency note for Azure OpenAI (linked from the data privacy page; not cached).

incidents.value: Vendor notice (Feb 2025): the Storm-2139 group used customer credentials scraped from public sources to abuse Azure OpenAI; Microsoft sued the actors (E.D. Va., Dec 2024; allegations, not ruled). No regulator decision found.

evidence.quote: Members of Storm-2139 exploited exposed customer credentials scraped from public sources to unlawfully access accounts with certain generative AI services.

incidents.note: Microsoft is the plaintiff; the case concerns misuse of leaked customer keys, not a breach of Microsoft systems. One web search for Azure OpenAI breaches or fines; press-only reports not used.
